mentions.name: Plates
mentions.description: A completely native iPhone weightlifting logging app built with SwiftUI/UIKit. It focuses on native UI elements, including custom keyboards for plate-loaded exercises and RPE/RIR inputs, native animations, and haptic feedback. The app has no backend servers and no tracking SDKs, yet supports cross-device sync via Apple's CloudKit, and is offered as a one-time payment instead of a subscription.
mentions.problem: Worthwhile iPhone weightlifting apps require a monthly payment for a full feature set while delivering an uninspiring, cross-platform experience that doesn't feel native to the iPhone.
mentions.source_excerpt: Out of my love for weightlifting I then shipped Plates and have been working on it ever since. It's a completely native iPhone lifting app (SwiftUI/UIKit) and I've gone quite hard on native UI elements such as custom keyboards for plate-loaded exercises and RPE/RIR inputs, native animations, and nice haptic feel. It has no backend servers and no tracking SDKs, yet it still supports things like cross-device sync thanks to Apple's CloudKit. The best part is that it's just a one-time payment.

mentions.name: Plates: Weightlifting Log
mentions.description: Plates: Weightlifting Log is a fully native weightlifting tracking app that logs workouts and provides training insights such as a muscle heatmap, 1RM breakdowns with different formulas, working volume, and best volume. It is a one-time purchase of $12.99, built natively rather than with cross-platform frameworks so it feels at home on the device.
mentions.problem: Existing workout trackers are mostly built with cross-platform frameworks like React Native or Flutter so they never feel truly native on the device, and nothing met the author's bar; there is a gap in the prosumer market for a fully native, ownable tool.
mentions.audience: Prosumer weightlifters who already know what they're doing in the gym, have their program, and want a solid tool they can actually own.
mentions.source_excerpt:
i wanted to build something for people who already know what they're doing in the gym, have their program, and just want a solid tool they can actually own (it's a one-time purchase of $12.99) that at the same time gives them all the insights they'd reasonably want (muscle heatmap, 1rm breakdowns with different formulas, working volume, best volume, etc.).

the app is called Plates: Weightlifting Log. if you're interested in checking it out: https://useplates.com
